before.html:
Question 1
?

If f(x)=cos⁡x10x2, find f′(x).

a
sin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x3
b
x2sin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x3
c
sin⁡x−cos⁡x10x3
d
−xsin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x3
e
xsin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x4
Submit

decision.explanation: Write f(x)=(1/10)x^{-2}cos(x). By the product rule, f'(x)=(1/10)[-2x^{-3}cos(x)-x^{-2}sin(x)]=[-x sin(x)-2cos(x)]/(10x^3), so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=cos⁡x$ and $v(x)=10{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-sin⁡x)(10{x}^{2})-(cos⁡x)(20x)}{(10{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10{x}^{2}sin⁡x-20xcos⁡x}{100{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{10x}(-xsin⁡x-2cos⁡x)}{\cancel{10x}\cdot 10{x}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-xsin⁡x-2cos⁡x}{10{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

If f(x)=cos⁡x10x2, find f′(x).

a
sin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x3
b
x2sin⁡x−2cos⁡x10x3

EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=cos⁡x and v(x)=10x2.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

content.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=cos⁡x$ and $v(x)=10{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-sin⁡x)(10{x}^{2})-(cos⁡x)(20x)}{(10{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10{x}^{2}sin⁡x-20xcos⁡x}{100{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{10x}(-xsin⁡x-2cos⁡x)}{\cancel{10x}\cdot 10{x}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{-xsin⁡x-2cos⁡x}{10{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=cos⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({e}^{x})^{′}\cdot cos⁡x-{e}^{x}\cdot (cos⁡x)^{′}}{(cos⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}cos⁡x+{e}^{x}sin⁡x}{(cos⁡x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x}(cos⁡x+sin⁡x)}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let $u=sin⁡x$ and $v=x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =cos⁡x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x(cos⁡x)-sin⁡x\cdot (1)}{(x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{xcos⁡x-sin⁡x}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Quotient Using Leibniz Notation
content.worked_solution:
Let $u=sin⁡x$ and $v=x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =cos⁡x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x(cos⁡x)-sin⁡x\cdot (1)}{(x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{xcos⁡x-sin⁡x}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{sin⁡x}{2x},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
after.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=sin⁡x$ and $v(x)=2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(sin⁡x)^{′}\cdot (2x)-sin⁡x\cdot (2x)^{′}}{(2x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{cos⁡x\cdot (2x)-sin⁡x\cdot 2}{{(2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(xcos⁡x-sin⁡x)}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{xcos⁡x-sin⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{\pi cos⁡(\pi )-sin⁡(\pi )}{2(\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\pi (-1)-(0)}{2{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\frac{1}{2\pi }.$

content.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{sin⁡x}{2x},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
content.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=sin⁡x$ and $v(x)=2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(sin⁡x)^{′}\cdot (2x)-sin⁡x\cdot (2x)^{′}}{(2x)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{cos⁡x\cdot (2x)-sin⁡x\cdot 2}{{(2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(xcos⁡x-sin⁡x)}{4{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{xcos⁡x-sin⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{\pi cos⁡(\pi )-sin⁡(\pi )}{2(\pi )^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\pi (-1)-(0)}{2{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2{\pi }^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\frac{1}{2\pi }.$

$$

$$
